body:
Instead of deleting a single line at a time when the scrollback is full
in terminal mode, will delete 10% of the lines.

Is a partial solution (workaround?) to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/8811

comment_data.body: maybe this if-block can go out of the while-loop, and the while-loop can become a for-loop. And then `appended_lines` could also be moved out of the loop.

I'm not sure that `xfree` is wanted here. Note that `on_scrollback_option_changed` does that because when the actual 'scrollback' option changes we want libvterm's internal scrollback to change. But not here.

Here (in `refresh_scrollback`) we're only updating the vim (user-facing) buffer.

> I'm not sure that xfree is wanted here.

I see... but the memory is still being allocated to libvterm's internal scrollback. Doesn't it bother us? Or `on_scrollback_option_changed` should take care of that?

> but the memory is still being allocated to libvterm's internal scrollback

yes but that allocation isn't done by `refresh_scrollback` , it's done elsewhere, and also freed elsewhere (`terminal_destroy`), just as before this PR.

> yes but that allocation isn't done by refresh_scrollback , it's done elsewhere, and also freed elsewhere (terminal_destroy), just as before this PR.

Thanks for explaining
@danielBelenky It's wrong, but it doesn't matter right now. What matters is getting it to actually work, without failing the ASan build (the first build listed in Travis CI).

comment_regular_data.body: This means the scrollback is effectively only 90% what the user requested. Wouldn't it be less disturbing if nvim instead collected lines _in addition_ (which could be less than 10% for a large scrollback), so a larger delete could be done _down_ to the user requested size?

> This means the scrollback is effectively only 90% what the user requested.

Right. Maybe it is not the best idea to blindly delete 10% of the scrollback.

> Wouldn't it be less disturbing if nvim instead collected lines in addition (which could be less than 10% for a large scrollback), so a larger delete could be done down to the user requested size?

I'm not sure I fully understand your suggestion... You want to delete 10% but only up to the user's definition?

@danielBelenky I mean we should let the scrollback buffer grow slightly larger than the users requested size, so we can do a large delete, without going below the requested size. If the user requested 1000 lines, it is better to delete from 1100 down to 1000, than from 1000 down to 900.

That seems good. So just set `sb_size` to 'scrollback' + 10% extra at https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/6ec9d790e11b009a8c002987bdbcb6250848aad5/src/nvim/terminal.c#L252-L253

something like this:

```c
int scbk_plus_10pct = (int)((double)curbuf->b_p_scbk * 1.10);
rv->sb_size = curbuf->b_p_scbk < 0
                ? SB_MAX : (size_t)MAX(1, scbk_plus_10pct);
```

Note: in the case of `SB_MAX`, don't bother with 10% extra.

> exit the loop that executes `ml_delete` when `buf->b_ml.ml_line_count - height <= term->sb_size`

👍  Makes sense to me.
Still want something like this probably, but needs tests. And I think https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39773 does something like this.
